about: The importer for a C-CDA document downloaded from a patient portal: it hands the file on whole for an import, with what the document's header says. pod.look() and pod.import() call it; an app does not.
capabilities: Recognising a downloaded C-CDA document · ccdaDownload.documents(), isCdaDocument()
Saying what a C-CDA document's header states · CcdaDocument.facts()
Listing a C-CDA document's entries before an import · ccdaDownload.index(), dateOrUtcTimeOf()
Finding whose records a C-CDA document holds · scopesOf()

glossary.definition: the program that converts an export into records; `import` loads it on first use.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's XML standard for clinical documents, whose root element is `ClinicalDocument`. C-CDA is the set of CDA templates US patient portals use.
a time as CDA writes it: `YYYYMMDD`, then optionally hours, minutes and seconds, then optionally an offset from UTC, such as `20250403083000-0400`.
the organisation that keeps a document and answers for its true copy.
one file that an import takes whole and gives to an adapter: a FHIR resource or Bundle in JSON, or a C-CDA document. The pod keeps its bytes.
a file of a person's records as a hospital's server or portal gave it, before any import: FHIR resources in JSON, or a C-CDA document.
in CDA, an identifier in two parts: a `root`, an OID or a UUID that says who issued it, and an optional `extension`, the value that issuer gave.
the part of the runtime that knows one form of export: it says which files are its documents and what the export states about each. `pod.look()` and `pod.import()` try each importer in turn.
one thing `index()` lists for `pod.look()` to count: something an import would bring, with its source's name, its kind or section, and when it was received, each only where the export states it.
the standard name of a file's format, such as `application/fhir+json`; an import offers a document to the adapters of its media type.
National Provider Identifier: the ten-digit number the US government gives each provider of health care; in CDA an id whose root is `2.16.840.1.113883.4.6`.
CDA's attribute that says a value is absent and why, such as `UNK` for unknown; an id that carries one identifies nothing.
the person an export's records are about, as that source knows them, before anyone has said who they are in the pod.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
the two ids a record from a C-CDA document is named under: one of the document's custodian and one of its patient. Two downloads with the same scope give the same record the same name.
one titled part of a C-CDA document's body, such as Medications or Allergies, holding an `entry` element for each coded record.
